item.description: House Democrats will hold leadership elections on Nov. 18.

item.title: House fire in Brooklyn kills 6 people, injures 7, more than 200 firefighters respond
item.description: A fire in a two-story home in New York has killed six people and injured seven others

item.title: Bomb threats cause major flight disruptions across Europe
item.description: Bomb ​threats forced airliners to make unplanned landings across Europe on Thursday morning, the latest in a series of threats targeting flights in Europe. While no country has attributed blame for the threats, they come at a time ​when European officials have been blaming both Russia and Iran for what they describe as "hybrid attacks" and acts of sabotage. Moscow and Tehran both deny any such campaign. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle tells us more.

item.title: US midterms: Elon Musk fails $440 million bet as Republicans lose
item.description: The 2026 midterm elections were the most expensive on record, with nearly 12 billion dollars spent during the campaign. Tech tycoon Elon Musk was by far the largest individual donor ever, injecting over 440 million dollars of his money to support the GOP. Tuesday's resounding Democratic victory showed the limits of his money, power and influence.

item.title: Hong Kong activist jailed for 10 more years for collusion with foreign forces
item.description: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 more years in jail on Thursday for colluding with foreign powers, the second time he has been penalised under the city's national security law. Hong, 30, is one of the most globally recognised faces of Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement and has already spent almost six years behind bars. He is now not due for release until late 2036.

item.title: Route du Rhum 2026: Sailors forced to abandon race for various reasons
item.description: The 2026 Route du Rhum is continuing to deliver one setback after another since Sunday’s start in Saint-Malo. From boats capsizing to sailors being forced to abandon the race, the favourites are dropping out one by one. But how do so many boats suffer damage so early in the race?

item.title: US Midterms: Democrats say ready to negotiate and promise big changes
item.description: US Democrats are promising to leverage their landslide election win to bring down living costs and hold President Donald Trump's administration to account. They are set to take control of both chambers of Congress in January, but delivering on their agenda could mean striking deals with the very president they have pledged to rein in.

item.title: Houthi missiles fired at Medina intercepted, Saudi coalition says
item.description: A ballistic missile fired at the Saudi city of Medina, one of Islam's holiest cities, was intercepted Thursday, a spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthi rebels said. The announcement came shortly after the kingdom's civil defence agency warned of potential danger around the strategic port of Yanbu.

item.title: Who won the redistricting war? So far, it looks like Democrats
item.description: Dems were able to keep seats that Republicans redrew to make them GOP-friendly.

item.title: South Africans eager to vote as local elections put failing services in focus
item.description: South Africans voted on Wednesday, November 4, in local elections. Nearly 30 million people were eligible to cast their ballots, with corruption, failing infrastructure and the deterioration of essential services among the key issues shaping the vote. FRANCE 24's correspondent Eunice Masson reports from the ground.

item.title: Football legend Cristiano Ronaldo announces international retirement
item.description: Portuguese football legend Cristiano Ronaldo announced on Thursday that he was retiring from international football. This is a breaking news story, more details to come.

item.title: Sudan accuses Ethiopia of allowing RSF drone launches from its territory
item.description: Sudan accused Ethiopia of allowing the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to launch drones from its territory. What does this allegation reveal about the RSF's military capabilities and foreign backing? FRANCE 24 spoke to Ali Mahmoud Ali, a Sudan researcher at ACLED, the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project, which monitors conflicts worldwide.

item.title: WATCH: The wide-ranging reactions to election night
item.description: After an Election Day so pivotal that votes were even being cast from space, there were many expressive reactions shared online.

item.title: Ethiopian families fleeing conflict face difficulties with food access
item.description: A renewed conflict in Ethiopia has led to the displacement of thousands of civilians. But after years of war in the country and heavy budget cuts, humanitarian organisations have all but left many of the camps for internally displaced people, leaving many without food or health care. FRANCE 24's correspondent Tom Canetti reports.

item.title: Dozens dead and missing after Russian strike on Ukrainian aid centre
item.description: The death toll from a Russian bombing of an aid distribution point in Ukraine's southeastern Zaporizhzhia region on Monday has risen to 42, with dozens still missing, officials said, in one of the deadliest strikes on civilians this year. The attack came a day ​after a brief ‌US-brokered local ceasefire expired and less than a week before the United States is due to bring together Ukrainian and Russian delegations ⁠in Abu Dhabi for talks on ending the war, now in its fifth year.

item.title: Zelensky in Spain for talks with world leaders as Kyiv seeks to strengthen air defences
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky made a surprise visit to Madrid on Wednesday to drum up fresh military support against Russia during a summit of Latin American leaders in Spain. Madrid is hosting a two-day summit of the Ibero-American Community, a 22-nation group of Spanish and Portuguese-speaking countries where support for Ukraine since Russia's 2022 invasion has divided opinion. FRANCE 24's Kyiv correspondent, Emmanuelle Chaze reports.

item.title: Israel president urges compromise after divisive election
item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday accepted the certified results of last week’s parliamentary elections as legally binding and began consultations with party representatives on forming a new government. Herzog began consultations with party leaders on Wednesday night to determine whom to designate to form a government — a process that could bring Netanyahu’s opponents to power.

item.title: After midterm stinging defeat, Trump is left to weigh his next move in Iran war
item.description: As he takes stock of his Republican Party's midterm drubbing, US President Donald Trump now faces the difficult question of what to do about his unpopular war against Iran. Trump acknowledged the war affected the midterms, suggesting voters were frustrated by surging gas prices that have been a byproduct of the more than 8-month-old conflict. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle tells us more.

item.title: Cyberattack hits French blood bank site, no blood products compromised
item.description: A cyberattack on several blood banks tried to raise temperatures to extremely high levels but was thwarted before it could do any damage to blood products or samples, French authorities said. The incident comes after supermarkets in a number of European countries reported this week that their fridges and freezers warmed up after they were remotely taken over, resulting in tons of spoiled food at a total cost of millions of euros.

item.title: Students blockade schools, universities as France braces for mass rallies
item.description: Students blockaded dozens of high schools and universities across France on Tuesday to maintain pressure on the government over education reforms, as trade unions prepared for a nationwide strike. The school protests have fuelled a broader movement against soaring prices and inadequate public services, which has drawn hundreds of thousands of people onto the streets over the past three weekends. FRANCE 24's Clovis Casali reports from a high school blockaded by students in Aubervilliers, near Paris.

item.title: Judges to hear Trump's appeal of 2024 criminal hush money conviction
item.description: Two and a half years after a jury convicted Donald Trump of 34 felony counts in his hush money case, the president's lawyers are seeking to have the verdict overturned.

item.title: Trump's arch is on the verge of federal approval. But a judge could block construction
item.description: A federal panel will meet to consider the arch for final approval on Thursday, and the government said it may begin construction later that same day. Critics hope a judge will intervene last-minute.

item.title: Does the blue wave mean lower gasoline and diesel prices soon? Don't hold your breath
item.description: A new Democratic majority in Congress could pressure the president to end the war in Iran. But it will be harder for them to directly affect fuel prices, which are tied to a complex international oil market. (Image credit: Tony Gutierrez)

item.title: The South flexes political power in midterms, sets regional influence in 2028 election
item.description: Tuesday's dramatic midterm results have transformed the electoral map, ensuring the path to future power for Democrats and Republicans must run through the South and its diverse voting population. (Image credit: Megan Varner)

item.title: As budgets tighten, people are breaking out their library cards
item.description: Some Americans squeezed by high prices are relying more on their local libraries for things like books, streaming services and high-priced items like musical instruments and sewing machines. (Image credit: Michael M. Santiago)

item.title: Poundland owner turns to Thames Water creditors' lobbying firm as political heat rises
item.description: The embattled owner of Poundland has parachuted in a team of top London lobbyists as it faces intensifying political pressure over the discount retailer's fate.

item.title: 'Wild west' e-bike parking targeted - with possibility of locally set fees
item.description: The government is seeking to end "wild west" e-bike parking and crack down on antisocial behaviour, such as riding on pavements.

item.title: Dublin-Rome flight diverted to French military base over bomb threat
item.description: An Airbus A320 ​flying from Dublin to Rome was safely diverted to France's Evreux airbase ​following a ‌bomb threat, ⁠the French prime minister's office said Thursday, in the latest in a series ‌of threats targeting flights across Europe. Multiple other flights in Europe also made emergency landings after being diverted because of bomb threats, authorities said.

item.title: Champions League: Lens suffer historic 9-1 defeat against Como
item.description: RC Lens suffered the heaviest defeat in the history of French football in European competition, losing 9-1 at home to Como in the Champions League. Having already been beaten by Club Brugge (3-0) and Sporting CP (2-0), Lens have now suffered three consecutive defeats in Europe.

item.title: Third person charged after police officer shot in foot in Nottingham
item.description: A 31-year-old woman has become the third person to be charged after a police officer was shot in the foot at a bus stop in Nottingham city centre.

item.title: Bob Dylan comes knockin' on pope's door as Leo welcomes legend to Vatican
item.description: The American singer-songwriter and poet visited with the American pope at the Vatican during a break between concert dates in Italy. The Vatican said the encounter was brief. (Image credit: Vatican Media/LaPresse)

item.title: France braces for fresh protests in test for Macron's policies
item.description: Hundreds of thousands of protesters are expected to march through French cities and public workers to strike on Thursday, in a fresh test for President Emmanuel Macron after weeks of ​unrest that have rattled ‌his government and dominated the agenda five months ahead of a presidential election.

item.title: Live: French unions stage nationwide strike in fresh test for Macron’s policies
item.description: French trade unions joined forces on Thursday for nationwide strikes and demonstrations for higher wages and in support of the high school protest movement, piling new pressure on the beleaguered government. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in prison
item.description: Wong was sentenced for his second conviction under a Beijing-imposed national security law, in a case that critics say reflects the crackdown on the city's once-thriving pro-democracy movement. (Image credit: Vincent Yu)

item.description: A student-run automotive shop has opened to the public – giving high schoolers hands-on experience with oil changes, tire rotations and multi-point inspections.

item.title: Melania Trump to host Ukrainian, Russian officials at White House
item.description: Russian and Ukrainian officials, including human rights chiefs, are set to meet US First Lady Melania Trump at the White House Thursday ahead of Abu Dhabi talks aimed at ending the Ukraine war. It comes weeks after Melania Trump helped broker a partial ceasefire enabling the evacuation of civilians from the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky.

item.title: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong gets 10 more years in jail for foreign collusion
item.description: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 more years in prison on Thursday for colluding with foreign powers, a court summary said. Wong, 30, pleaded guilty in September to seeking foreign sanctions against Hong Kong and China under Beijing’s national security law, having spent nearly six years imprisoned.

item.title: UK agrees to 'time-bound' talks on harms of slave trade
item.description: The UK has agreed to engage in "structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith" talks that address the "historical harms" of the transatlantic slave trade, Commonwealth leaders have said.
